prisoner.name: Yukio Eto
prisoner.description: Yukio Eto was a Japanese American participant in the Heart Mountain draft-resistance movement. After being confined at Heart Mountain during World War II, he was prosecuted for refusing military conscription and imprisoned at McNeil Island in Washington.

cases.charges: Violation of the Selective Training and Service Act — Heart Mountain draft resistance
cases.sentence: 2 years imposed. Served time at McNeil Island in Washington. Actual release date has not been established.

entries.custody_evidence: 1944/1945 draft prosecution; identified on McNeil Island December 1946 prisoner-release planning list. Scheduled dates not entered as actual releases.
entries.map_note: Approximate Heart Mountain protest/camp location (Yale); not a current address. Prison linked separately when established.

prisoner.name: Fred Homi Iriye
prisoner.description: Fred Homi Iriye was a Japanese American draft resister confined at Heart Mountain and later imprisoned at McNeil Island. He refused conscription while his community was deprived of its civil rights. In 1946 he was electrocuted while working in the prison power plant, shortly before his planned release.

cases.charges: Violation of the Selective Training and Service Act — Heart Mountain draft resistance
cases.sentence: Three years imposed. Imprisoned at McNeil Island, where he worked in the power plant. He died by electrocution in custody in 1946, shortly before a planned release. The precise date of death has not been established.

entries.custody_evidence: Original 1944 prison admission plus museum account of death while working in prison in 1946.
research_notes: Arrest day conflicts: museum April 7, prison summary April 6. Retain April 1944 precision. Do not equate planned release with death date.
entries.map_note: Approximate Heart Mountain protest/camp location (Yale); not a current address. Prison linked separately when established.

prisoner.description: Roy Masao Uyeda was a Japanese American participant in the Heart Mountain draft-resistance movement. After being confined at Heart Mountain during World War II, he was prosecuted for refusing military conscription and imprisoned at McNeil Island in Washington.

cases.charges: Violation of the Selective Training and Service Act — Heart Mountain draft resistance
cases.sentence: 2 years imposed. Served time at McNeil Island in Washington. Actual release date has not been established.

prisoner.name: Torao Uyemura
prisoner.description: Torao Uyemura resisted conscription while confined at Heart Mountain, arguing that his citizenship rights had not been clarified. He pleaded not guilty to failing to report for a pre-induction physical, was convicted, and was imprisoned at McNeil Island in 1944.

cases.charges: Violation of the Selective Training and Service Act — Heart Mountain draft resistance
cases.sentence: Three years imposed; the prison admission summary records commitment to McNeil Island on July 10, 1944 and continued custody in August 1944. Its projected conditional-release date is not evidence of actual release.

entries.custody_evidence: Original prison admission summary: committed July 10, 1944; still in custody August 7, 1944.
